samples.summary: Link-exit guards trust a pending style without checking its anchor, so a *stale* `href: undefined` gets re-anchored to a new caret position and unlinks text typed inside a link
samples.evidence: `pendingStyleFor` (editor.ts:1193-1197) does `const prev = pending.get(); ... !!(prev && 'href' in prev && prev.href === undefined)` — it never compares the pending anchor with `cursor.position`. `createPendingStyle` (view/pending-style.ts:28-42) deliberately self-protects against staleness: `consumeForInsert` nulls the state when `state.anchor` doesn't match the insert offset, so a pending style left over from another position is normally discarded and never applied. The new guards defeat that: they read the stale flag and then `pending.set(..., cursor.position)`, re-anchoring the exit to the *current* caret. Caret moves that clear pending (mousedown, arrows, Home/End, paste, copy/cut) hide this, but not all do — `EditorAPI.clearSearchMatches(true)` (editor.ts:3991-4000) moves the cursor and sets a range with no `pending.clear()`, and `restoreLocalCursor` (editor.ts:4356) likewise. Sequence: type at a link's trailing edge (pending armed with `href: undefined` by `exitLinkIfAtTrailingEdge`), jump the caret into the middle of another link via find/replace close, click Bold → pending now carries `href: undefined` at that interior caret, and the next typed character is unlinked, splitting the link. The identical unanchored `prev` test appears in `TextEditor.setPendingStyleGuarded` (text-editor.ts:3466-3469) and in `stepSelectionFontSizeImpl` (text-box-editor.ts:896-898, via `staged`).

samples.summary: Dropping the `position.offset > start` test makes `isAtLinkTrailingEdge` report a trailing edge at boundaries that carry no link at all
samples.evidence: The loop returns on the *first* inline whose `end === position.offset` and which has an `href`; with the `offset > start` test gone, a zero-length inline qualifies. For inlines `[{text:'abc', style:{}}, {text:'', style:{href:'A'}}, {text:'def', style:{}}]` a caret at offset 3 — plain text on both sides — now returns `true`, so `exitLinkIfAtTrailingEdge` and the three new guards arm a spurious `href: undefined` on the pending style. Harmless in itself (there is no href to strip), but it means the predicate no longer answers the question its name and doc comment state, and any future caller that treats `true` as 'the caret is just past a hyperlink' will be wrong.

samples.summary: Selection branch of the text-box `removeLink` skips the unconditional layout invalidation the caret branch performs
samples.evidence: The new branch delegates to `applyStyleImpl` (text-box-editor.ts:823-835), which only sets `layoutCache = undefined` when `doc.getBlockIndex()` resolves *both* endpoints (`if (startIdx >= 0 && endIdx >= 0)`). The pre-existing caret branch (text-box-editor.ts:1282) invalidates unconditionally. If a selection endpoint's block cannot be indexed, the href is written to the model but the cached layout is reused, so the removed link keeps painting with link styling until the next edit. Reachability of an unindexable block in a text box is unclear, hence low confidence, but the two branches of the same command now differ in their invalidation contract.
